summary: 12 example simulations fail, all in US-06.6 (the full tariff code). The failures look like one format mismatch: the computed code is split into parts such as ['N', 1, 'Y'], and the expected value is the joined string 'N1Y'. The 'no tariff code' cases return None. This story is the main acceptance test for the computed code, so it must pass before build. The step order is also contradictory between feature.md and US-01.2. Technical terms leak into business prose against D-045. The open questions are non-blocking, but the calculator comparison is a go-live condition.

findings.title: All US-06.6 examples fail (tariff code assembly)
findings.why: The full tariff code is the main output of the feature. Its acceptance examples do not pass, so the rule and the examples disagree. Most likely the rule returns the parts (letter, digit, church suffix) as a list instead of the joined string, and returns None where the spec says 'no tariff code'. The spec side could also be at fault.
findings.evidence: examples: AC-06.6.1 (6 cases), AC-06.6.2 (3 cases), AC-06.6.3 (3 cases). Example: tariff_code = ['N',1,'Y'], expected 'N1Y'. Example: tariff_code = None, expected 'no tariff code'. rule.tariff_letter: the cited fact maps G->Q, but the rule returns null for G.
findings.action: Fix the tariff_code expression so it joins letter, digit and suffix into one string. Decide how 'no tariff code' is represented, either null or an explicit marker, and align the example wording with that. Re-run the examples. Also resolve the G->Q handling in tariff_letter.

findings.title: Step order contradicts itself (8 vs 10 steps)
findings.why: Engineering cannot tell whether the Germany cross-border questions come before or after denomination and children. They also cannot tell whether there is a separate first-working-day step or a summary step.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement on feature.md: the flow table has 8 steps. The questionnaire_flow rule and AC-01.2.1 have 10 steps. trace_judge on rule.questionnaire_flow: the content of steps 1-5 and 7-10 is not backed by cited facts.
findings.action: Add a decision in decisions.yaml fixing the one authoritative step order. Regenerate feature.md and US-01.2 from it.

findings.title: Behaviour after an HR edit is undefined (US-01.6)
findings.why: If HR changes an answer so that new questions apply, those inputs were never asked. The derived tariff code and other results could be wrong or stale.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement on US-01.6 (major). Related: OQ-hr-side-follow-ups is non-blocking.
findings.action: Decide what derived results show while inputs are missing: no code, an 'incomplete' state, or the old value. Decide whether answers that no longer apply are discarded after an HR change, as they are on employee submission.

findings.title: Technical terms leak into business prose
findings.why: D-045 forbids internal rule ids and formula talk in the spec text.
findings.evidence: tech_leak in feature.md: '(discard_inapplicable_answers)' and '(read_only_after_submission)'. 'The expression ...' appears in feature.md and information.md, 2 times each.
findings.action: Reword in business language. Examples: 'each child adds 1 or 0 to the child count' and 'H applies if any child counts with H'. Remove the snake_case ids.

findings.title: Calculator coverage is unproven for unexplored and inferred paths
findings.why: Lonio now owns the tariff result. Unexplored paths could produce wrong codes. These are the residence block for A/B/H, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N, and the inferred child rows (US-07.3 to US-07.6).
findings.evidence: OQ-calculator-coverage (non-blocking). inferred_items: rule.child_result, rule.child_count, US-05.2, US-07.3 to US-07.6. fact_judge: partial on F-zh_source_tax_calculator-037b1c, 64ac33, dc0ae9, c8aa5e and 2754e8.
findings.action: Record a go-live condition: a domain expert compares the computed codes with the Zurich calculator. Confirm that the inferred rows are acceptable. Specify a maximum child count, or confirm 'no maximum'.

findings.title: Several claims are not backed by cited facts
findings.why: Traceability is weak for some rules. A reviewer cannot verify them from the sources.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: 'required' answers in US-07.1 to US-07.5. 'No maximum' children in AC-06.6.1. 'Children never change the letter for married employees' in US-06.4 and US-07.6. Uncited fact ids in calculator_residence, child_result and cross_border_tariff. The invented 01.04 date in US-03.3.
findings.action: Add the missing citations, or mark the items as inferred or decided via decisions.yaml. For example, cite D-034 and D-044. Remove or mark the invented example date.

findings.title: Source tax rule rests on hedged or unconfirmed statements
findings.why: The core rule for who is subject to source tax is built on a hedged answer from Anna ('I think so'), and the portal facts overstate what the units show.
findings.evidence: fact_judge: partial on F-hr_transcript-550840 and 5af8d0. Portal facts 39bab1 (spouse date of birth only when Married), 6d3630 and b359c3. Related open-question id OQ-source-tax-rule-confirmation appears in the changed elements.
findings.action: Get written confirmation from HR (Anna) of the final rule. Confirm what the portal does for Divorced and Widowed and for employees living abroad. Record the answers as decisions.

findings.title: Address required-fields and example inconsistencies
findings.why: The AC text and the examples disagree on which address fields are required. This produces ambiguous tests.
findings.evidence: US-02.2: AC-02.2.1 omits the house number, which D-042 makes required. The Germany example marks fields only 'asked'. US-05.2 and US-05.1 mix 'required' and 'asked'. US-01.2 shows civil status as '–' for Germany.
findings.action: Decide that all address fields are required, with 'no house number' as the only exception. Use one term ('required') in all examples. Fix the Germany civil-status example.

findings.title: Unspecified values and limits
findings.why: These are build-time decisions that nobody has made yet, and the spec does not cover them.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement info: permit reminder wording not given (US-01.4). Country and nationality list and stateless cases (US-05.1). Limits on the first working day and date of birth (US-03.1). Save and resume and confirmation (US-01.6). Spouse residence as yes/no under data minimisation (US-05.2). Keep-answers wording in D-036 versus AC-01.5.1.
findings.action: Record decisions: who provides the reminder wording and when, the country list, the date plausibility rules, and the save/confirm behaviour. Decide whether the spouse residence question is a yes/no or a country. Say whether keeping answers is a testable requirement.
